question.knowledge_point: Writing a Factorial in an Equivalent Form
question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $(k+2)!$ for any $k\ge 0?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the definition of factorial, we have 

$$
(k+2)!=(k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1.
$$

Now, applying the factorial definition to all but the first factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(k+2)! & =(k+2)\cdot \overset{(k+1)!}{\overset{⏞}{(k+1)\cdot k\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1}} \\  & =(k+2)\cdot (k+1)!\end{aligned}
$$
